narrative.overview: Asking is taking a number at a counter: you say what you need, get a ticket, someone attends you, and you are called when it is your turn to decide. Light laminate ground, enamel-blue dispenser, thermal-white tickets, one navy LED board; hyperlegible sans at generous sizes; plain Spanish.
keyCharacteristics: Colour is job-coded: one key colour per errand.
State is always icon plus word.
Pressable primary things have a thick darker bottom edge.
Tickets carry a big tabular number.

rules.name: The Key-Colour Rule
rules.body: An errand has exactly one colour from the four keys; reused for its chip and log icon only.

rules.name: The Amber Means You Rule
rules.body: Amber on a surface means a person is needed.

rules.name: The Word Beside Colour Rule
rules.body: Every state is an icon plus its word.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is weight 800 versus 400-600 in one family.

rules.name: The LED Only Rule
rules.body: Doto appears only inside LED number displays.

rules.name: The Press Edge Rule
rules.body: Pressable primary objects get a solid deep-colour bottom edge; shadows are for objects you read.

dos: Do pair every state with its icon and word.
Do give primary pressable objects the solid deep-colour bottom edge.
Do keep the board's columns fixed and right-align times.
Do keep targets at least about 48px with a visible focus ring.
donts: Don't show tool names, models, paths, costs or permission jargon.
Don't convey state by colour alone.
Don't use key colours or amber outside their roles.
Don't use Doto outside LED numbers.
Don't open a modal for anything but a blocking decision.
